questions.prompt: Define a physical quantity.
questions.answer: A quantity that has a numerical value (magnitude) and a unit.

questions.prompt: State what is needed to fully give the value of a physical quantity.
questions.answer: Its numerical value together with its unit.

questions.prompt: State an estimate for the mass of an adult.
questions.answer: About 70 kg (accept 50–100 kg).

questions.prompt: State an estimate for the speed of a person walking.
questions.answer: About 1.5 m s⁻¹ (accept 1–2 m s⁻¹).

questions.prompt: State an estimate for the density of water.
questions.answer: About 1000 kg m⁻³.

questions.prompt: State an estimate for atmospheric pressure at sea level.
questions.answer: About 1 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.prompt: State the six S.I. base quantities and their units.
questions.answer: Mass (kg), length (m), time (s), electric current (A), thermodynamic temperature (K) and amount of substance (mol).

questions.prompt: State the S.I. base unit of mass.
questions.answer: The kilogram (kg).

questions.prompt: State the S.I. base unit of electric current.
questions.answer: The ampere (A).

questions.prompt: State the S.I. base unit of thermodynamic temperature.
questions.answer: The kelvin (K).

questions.prompt: Name the S.I. base quantity measured in moles.
questions.answer: Amount of substance.

questions.prompt: State the symbol for the S.I. base unit of length.
questions.answer: m (the metre).

questions.prompt: Define a derived unit.
questions.answer: A unit formed by combining S.I. base units.

questions.prompt: State the newton in terms of S.I. base units.
questions.answer: kg m s⁻².

questions.prompt: State the joule in terms of S.I. base units.
questions.answer: kg m² s⁻².

questions.prompt: State the watt in terms of S.I. base units.
questions.answer: kg m² s⁻³.

questions.prompt: State the pascal in terms of S.I. base units.
questions.answer: kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.prompt: State what is meant by checking the homogeneity of a physical equation using S.I. base units.
questions.answer: Checking that the base units of both sides of the equation are identical.

questions.prompt: Explain why an equation cannot be correct if the units on each side are different.
questions.answer: The two sides must be equal, so they must have the same units; different units mean the equation is not dimensionally consistent.

questions.prompt: State the symbol and value of the prefixes pico, nano and micro.
questions.answer: pico (p) = 10⁻¹², nano (n) = 10⁻⁹, micro (μ) = 10⁻⁶.

questions.prompt: State the symbol and value of the prefixes milli, centi and deci.
questions.answer: milli (m) = 10⁻³, centi (c) = 10⁻², deci (d) = 10⁻¹.

questions.prompt: State the symbol and value of the prefixes kilo, mega, giga and tera.
questions.answer: kilo (k) = 10³, mega (M) = 10⁶, giga (G) = 10⁹, tera (T) = 10¹².

questions.prompt: State the convention for labelling a graph axis.
questions.answer: Write the quantity divided by its unit, e.g. speed / m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: State the convention for a table column heading.
questions.answer: Write the quantity divided by its unit, e.g. time / s.

questions.prompt: State how the unit of the gradient of a graph is found from its axes.
questions.answer: Divide the unit of the quantity on the y-axis by the unit of the quantity on the x-axis.

title: Systematic and random errors, precision and accuracy

questions.prompt: Define a systematic error.
questions.answer: A constant offset that shifts every reading by the same amount in the same direction, e.g. a zero error.

questions.prompt: Define a random error.
questions.answer: An unpredictable variation in readings about the true value, differing in size and sign each time.

questions.prompt: State how random errors can be reduced.
questions.answer: Take repeated readings and calculate the average.

questions.prompt: Define precision.
questions.answer: How close repeated measurements are to each other (the size of the random spread).

questions.prompt: Define accuracy.
questions.answer: How close a measured value is to the true value.

questions.prompt: State the effect of a systematic error on accuracy and precision.
questions.answer: It reduces accuracy but not precision; all readings are shifted by the same amount.

questions.prompt: Define absolute uncertainty.
questions.answer: The uncertainty in a measurement expressed in the same units as the measurement, e.g. 2.0 ± 0.1 cm.

questions.prompt: State how percentage uncertainty is calculated from absolute uncertainty.
questions.answer: Percentage uncertainty = (absolute uncertainty ÷ measured value) × 100%.

questions.prompt: State the rule for combining uncertainties when two quantities are added or subtracted.
questions.answer: Add their absolute uncertainties.

questions.prompt: State the rule for combining uncertainties when two quantities are multiplied or divided.
questions.answer: Add their percentage uncertainties.

questions.prompt: State the rule for combining uncertainties when a quantity is raised to a power.
questions.answer: Multiply the percentage uncertainty by the power.

questions.prompt: A length is measured as 20.0 ± 0.5 cm. Calculate its percentage uncertainty.
State what the error bars on a graph represent.
questions.answer: The range of uncertainty of each data point.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by the line of best fit.
questions.answer: A line drawn so that data points are balanced above and below it and it passes through as many error bars as possible.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by the worst line on a graph.
questions.answer: The steepest or shallowest line that is still consistent with all the error bars.

questions.prompt: State how the uncertainty in a gradient is estimated from a graph.
questions.answer: Take half the difference between the gradients of the steepest and shallowest acceptable lines.

questions.prompt: State how percentage difference between an experimental value and an accepted value is calculated.
questions.answer: Percentage difference = (difference between the values ÷ accepted value) × 100%.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by an anomalous result and what should be done with it.
questions.answer: A point that does not fit the trend; it should be ignored when drawing the line of best fit.

questions.prompt: Define a scalar quantity.
questions.answer: A quantity with magnitude only.

questions.prompt: Define a vector quantity.
questions.answer: A quantity with both magnitude and direction.

questions.prompt: Give two examples of scalar quantities and two examples of vector quantities.
questions.answer: Scalars: e.g. speed, mass, energy, time. Vectors: e.g. velocity, force, displacement, acceleration.

questions.prompt: State the difference between distance and displacement.
questions.answer: Distance is a scalar and is the total path length; displacement is a vector and is the straight-line distance from start to finish with its direction.

questions.prompt: State how two vectors are added to find their resultant.
questions.answer: Place them tip to tail; the resultant is the vector from the tail of the first to the head of the second.

questions.prompt: State how a vector is subtracted from another vector.
questions.answer: Reverse the direction of the vector being subtracted, then add it tip to tail.

questions.prompt: State how a vector triangle is used to find the resultant of two coplanar vectors.
questions.answer: Draw the two vectors tip to tail; the resultant is the third side, from the tail of the first vector to the head of the second.

questions.prompt: State the equation for the horizontal component of a force F acting at an angle θ to the horizontal.
questions.answer: Fx = F cos θ.

questions.prompt: State the equation for the vertical component of a force F acting at an angle θ to the horizontal.
questions.answer: Fy = F sin θ.

questions.prompt: State what θ represents in the equation Fx = F cos θ.
questions.answer: The angle between the force and the horizontal (x-axis).

questions.prompt: Define resolving a vector.
questions.answer: Splitting a vector into two perpendicular components.

questions.prompt: State how the magnitude of the resultant of two perpendicular components is calculated.
questions.answer: Using Pythagoras: R = √(Fx² + Fy²).

questions.prompt: State how the magnitude of the resultant of two forces changes as the angle between them increases.
questions.answer: It decreases (for forces of fixed magnitude).
